historical.title: ALIVE-12 - Personal Research Intelligence
historical.text:
ALIVE-12 - Personal Research Intelligence
Engineering: PASS. Native synthetic: PASS. Native Meta: NOT RUN. Retrieval advantage: NOT DEMONSTRATED.
Baseline: d58c30748a5ec9273a0be86dc769d8c1b7dc6b23 (ALIVE-11-R1 merge). Branch: codex/alive-12-research-intelligence. Source commit for the evidence: cf7022cb168b4cbd65bbc0b98faafbb25b498c85. No paid inference was used.
Connections and feedback
POST /research/connections builds a deterministic candidate from lexical overlap between the current reviewed excerpt and the historical excerpt:
at least two shared content terms: same_concept, status candidate;
one shared term: complementary, status candidate, weak;
no shared term or missing exact quotation: insufficient_evidence, aborted connection.
Every candidate stores both source URLs and hashes, the current and historical quotations, exact quote-validation flags, shared terms, relation type and explanation. It is never labelled factual support. Connection feedback is persisted separately and never used to suppress a topic.

current.title: ALIVE-13 - Reliable Research Retrieval and Evidence-Grounded Connections
current.text:
ALIVE-13 - Reliable Research Retrieval and Evidence-Grounded Connections
What was wrong
ALIVE-12 established the research-memory lifecycle, but its retrieval path was:
goal + current text -> unscoped MemoryService top-k -> post-filter by research metadata
The rank and limit were therefore decided before goal and record-type eligibility. Sixty older ordinary memories could fill the candidate window before the relevant research row was considered. The same shared MemoryService path was also used by general cognition, so a saved research excerpt could enter an ordinary investigation prompt. The panel's withdrawal command used the last saved research ID rather than the displayed result. Lexical overlap was labelled same_concept or complementary, which overstated what shared words establish.
The frozen pre-fix evidence is in archives/ALIVE-13/evidence/pre-fix-defects.json:
With 60 ordinary memories, the old path returned 15 ordinary candidates and zero research candidates; the relevant research memory was absent.
The old general retrieval path returned the research sentinel; the corrected default returned the ordinary experience memory and excluded the sentinel.
The old background worker withdrew research-B-last-saved when the displayed item was research-A-displayed; the corrected worker withdrew the displayed ID and rejected a request with no explicit ID.
Contradictory, unrelated and weakly related fixtures were labelled same_concept, complementary or no_supported_connection; the corrected labels are topic_overlap_candidate, weak_lexical_overlap and insufficient_evidence.
These controlled reproductions reconstruct the pre-fix algorithm against a fresh database: the old query, top-k and post-filter are copied from af12bc8, and the ALIVE-13 type allowlist is explicitly disabled. They are faithful reproductions of the defect, not a literal execution from a checkout made before the edits.

current.title: ALIVE-13 - Reliable Research Retrieval and Evidence-Grounded Connections
current.text:
ALIVE-13 - Reliable Research Retrieval and Evidence-Grounded Connections
Engineering: ENGINEERING_PASS. Native synthetic: NATIVE_SYNTHETIC_PASS. Native Meta: NATIVE_META_NOT_RUN. Controlled lexical retrieval: RETRIEVAL_ADVANTAGE_DEMONSTRATED on the frozen corpus. General semantic or owner-usefulness superiority: NOT DEMONSTRATED.
Baseline: af12bc88c91a85558873d01579dba93fdd6b1bbf (ALIVE-12 merge, origin/main). Branch: codex/alive-13-reliable-research. Product and harness commit for the archived evidence: d963d267c219d49e4dfab23cf838946b64c4b190. Archive commit: 04adadb. PR: https://github.com/ernanhughes/alive/pull/19 (draft, review-only). CI: all eight PR checks passed (backend Ubuntu/Windows, dashboard, first-contact PostgreSQL). No paid inference was used. No merge or auto-merge was requested.
Connection evidence semantics
New connection records use only lexical claim labels:
topic_overlap_candidate - at least two shared content terms and exact sentence spans in both sources.
weak_lexical_overlap - exactly one shared content term and exact sentence spans.
insufficient_evidence - no inspectable shared span; the connection abstains.
The record carries the current URL/SHA-256, historical URL/SHA-256, exact current and historical source sentences, separately labelled model evidence quotation, shared terms, an explicit evidence_policy, and quote-validation booleans. The explanation states that lexical overlap does not establish agreement, support, contradiction or corroboration. The panel labels source spans and the historical model quotation separately. Legacy persisted rows are not rewritten.

historical.title: ALIVE-11 — Live native intelligence qualification
historical.text:
ALIVE-11 — Live native intelligence qualification
Engineering: PASS_WITH_LIMITATIONS. Research: BEHAVIOUR_CHANGE_DEMONSTRATED. Owner utility advantage is unestablished.
Review-04 corrections
ALIVE-11-R1 corrects the presentation and interpretation issues found in ALIVE-REVIEW-04:
Feedback ratings were scripted operator branch interventions, not a user study.
ALIVE-11 contains two paid campaigns, 16 recorded calls, 8,732 charged tokens and approximately $0.023665 estimated spend.
All qualification pages were controlled excerpts; this is not arbitrary browsing or open-web adaptation.
The synthetic comparison demonstrates missed opportunities, not adaptive superiority.
Runtime identity is reported by the backend and compared against module/source hashes; it is not inherently trustworthy merely because the backend states it.
Lexical relevance accepts one matching content token. The negation example is one failure of that shallow rule, not a negation-specific defect.
The extension now clears stale note cost and feedback state on no-action, suppression and uncertainty, and repeated snapshots no longer advance the recovery counter.
The policy comparison and recommendation are in docs/ALIVE-11-R1.md; the production default was not changed by the decision replay.

current.title: ALIVE-14 - Evidence-Grounded Research Connections
current.text:
ALIVE-14 - Evidence-Grounded Research Connections
Engineering: ENGINEERING_PASS. Native synthetic: NATIVE_SYNTHETIC_PASS. Native Meta: NATIVE_META_NOT_RUN. Retrieval: RETRIEVAL_ADVANTAGE_DEMONSTRATED on the frozen held-out lexical corpus. Relationship usefulness: RELATIONSHIP_USEFULNESS_NOT_DEMONSTRATED. Owner ratings: SCRIPTED_ONLY (no human ratings collected).
Baseline: 3d81ce9a435d375ff6652bde07582d22a1eafdd6 (ALIVE-13 merge, origin/main). Branch: codex/alive-14-research-connections. Protocol freeze commit: bf0af924d75483fc1c06ea5f8621ab08c3950b98. Implementation commit for the archived evidence: 83852b2bdcccdef041c3e440dce3a2b22906ad0c. PR: https://github.com/ernanhughes/alive/pull/20 (draft, review-only). CI: all eight PR checks passed (backend Ubuntu/Windows, dashboard, first-contact PostgreSQL). No paid inference was used. No merge or auto-merge was requested.
Limitations
The corpus is lexical and controlled; no semantic paraphrase claim.
Retrieval labels are source-adequacy labels, not owner usefulness ratings.
ALIVE-14 improves MRR and rank-1 on the held-out corpus but not recall or precision over ALIVE-13.
The local stub is not Meta and cannot establish relationship usefulness.
No owner ratings or paid Meta calls were collected.
Real Meta requires a separate approval naming the exact model, payloads, call count, token caps, spend cap, abort conditions and data-redaction plan.
Additional relationship feedback revisions are stored as revisions, not independent ratings.
